title: Cost vs fidelity tradeoffs - personal notebook
content:
Rough brain-dump / sketchbook for feature exploration: dynamic fidelity selection and cost-smoothing for hosted API

Goal: let applications trade some output fidelity for large reductions in per-token cost without changing SDK surface. Provide small, measurable knobs and safe fallbacks.

Motivation / problem statements (why this matters):
- Customers (chatbots, assistants, search-re-rankers) repeatedly ask: how can we reduce cost without 1) breaking core UX and 2) increasing latency?
- Many workloads have large tail of short queries or permissive quality needs (e.g., summarization, code-explainers). If we could reduce model size or use quantized variants adaptively we save $$ at scale.
- Ops teams complain about noisy billing spikes when traffic changes; they'd prefer unit-economics smoothing and predictable burn.

Guiding principles (quick):
- Transparent: customers should see expected cost/fidelity tradeoffs in the console and API responses.
- Safe: automatic fallback to full-fidelity if quality drops below a threshold.
- Incremental: start with advisory suggestions + manual toggles, then automate.

Feature ideas (candidate list):
1) Fidelity Profiles (user-configurable)
   - Names: high, balanced, economize, debug
   - Controls: model family hint (e.g., llama-2-13b -> 13b-int8, 7b-int4; or full -> quantized), max_output_tokens, temperature caps, use_prefix_cache=true/false, beam_count limit, response-truncation heuristics
   - UI: small slider in Console with expected % cost savings estimate (ballpark)

2) Request-level Budgeting API param: "cost_budget_cents" (optional)
   - Server picks smallest profile that is compatible with budget given input length/complexity estimate
   - Return header with chosen-profile and estimated-quality-score

3) Runtime-adaptive pruning
   - If model sees input pattern that historically needs less fidelity (e.g., simple factual Qs), switch to cheaper variant mid-request (or for next request in session)
   - Use quick classifier (tiny transformer) to route

4) Autopruning for batched workloads
   - In Dedicated/Dedicated-like workloads, dynamically group similar fidelity requests to reduce wasted compute.

5) Quantization-aware rollouts + canary metrics
   - Automatic rollback if downstream evals degrade (micro-evals, user-specified golden prompts)

User stories (rough):
- As an ML engineer, I want a per-route fidelity profile so that low-risk chatbot flows use cheaper variants while critical flows use full-fidelity models.
- As a product manager, I want a console projection of expected monthly spend given adoption of an "economize" profile so I can evaluate ROI.
- As an SRE, I want an automatic safety rollback when quality regressions exceed X% to avoid user-visible incidents.

Metrics / signals to measure success:
- Unit cost per 1k tokens (primary) — target 20-40% reduction for 'economize' on common workloads
- Accuracy/QA delta per micro-eval set — target <3% drop vs baseline for balanced profile
- User impact: average session success rate 
- Latency p50/p95 — ensure balancer doesn't add >10% latency
- False positive fallback rate (automatic fallback triggered when not needed) <2%

Quick experiment matrix (MVP experiments):
MVP A: Manual fidelity profiles only (UI + SDK)
- 2 routes: chat-general (balanced) and debug-help (economize)
- Measure cost deltas over 2 weeks on internal traffic + control group
- Linked tasks: JIRA-INFR-3842 (instrumentation), GH PR 789 (runtime flags)

MVP B: Request-level budget param + classifier-based routing
- Build tiny classifier (100ms max) that predicts complexity bucket (low/med/high)
- Route low->7b-int4, med->13b-int8, high->full 70b (if available)
- A/B test on small customer cohort (opt-in)

MVP C: Auto rollback using micro-evals
- Define golden prompt set for each customer route (customer-supplied or default)
- If average BLEU/ROUGE/QSim drops > threshold, rollback to previous profile

Potential UX surfaces:
- Console: route-level fidelity slider with projected monthly savings and quality indicator
- API: new header X-Redwood-Fidelity-Profile and response metadata: chosen_profile, estimated_quality_score, fallback_reason(if any)
- SDK: convenience wrapper that exposes budget param and local simulator for cost/fidelity preview

Pitfalls and open questions (TODO):
- Q: How to estimate "expected quality" cheaply? Micro-evals are slow. Maybe use a learned proxy quality model that predicts similarity to reference or hallucination risk.
- Q: For streaming responses, can we switch mid-stream? Likely not safe; instead, tag session preference and switch next request.
- Q: How to prevent gaming: customers setting tiny budgets for sensitive endpoints? Need guardrails + hard limits per-route.
- Q: Billing model: should we bill by chosen model variant? by actual tokens delivered? by budget? Need finance input.

Implementation notes / runtime hooks (brainstorm):
- Add fidelity metadata to model catalog entries: {cost_score, size_tag, expected_latency, quality_profile_tags} (this is internal sketch, will become rows in model catalog)
- Router will consult policy: explicit route override -> per-request budget -> classifier -> fallback priority list
- Telemetry: every request logs (profile_chosen, estimated_quality_score, fallback, latency, tokens_in/out) to a new index for quick aggregation

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0: internal-only feature flag, manual profiles, console preview (2-4 weeks)
- Phase 1: external opt-in customers (GTM with Solutions) + add classifier routing (6-8 weeks)
- Phase 2: enable auto budget routing with safety rollback, add per-customer golden prompts and micro-eval hooks (3 months)

Acceptance criteria for initial launch (internal opt-in):
- Console slider + SDK param exist and documented in quickstart
- Runtime honors selected profile for 95% of requests (no silent overrides without warning)
- Basic telemetry emitted and dashboards present for cost, latency, fallback counts

Notes to self / short-term TODOs:
- [ ] Spike small classifier (pytorch) on internal chat logs, target 90% recall for "low complexity"
- [ ] Add catalog fields in GH PR 789 (runtime)
- [ ] Draft console wireframes and copy (ask Priya for help)
- [ ] Create micro-eval set template and share with Solutions (Noah)
- [ ] Quick call with Finance to discuss billing implications (schedule via Slack thread)

References / inspiration:
- Gated routing in large-scale ad systems (quality vs spend)
- Multi-fidelity sensor networks literature (dynamic sampling vs cost)
- Internal notes: cost-ladder-fallbacks sketch (Sophia) — different approach but overlapping concerns

Freeform thoughts:
- Could expose a "simulation" endpoint: give me X prompts -> simulate cost & predicted quality for N fidelity choices. Useful for customers to test without traffic change.
- For Dedicated customers, expose rent-a-quantization pipeline: they can choose to upload quantized weights that we certify and route to.
- Consider a marketplace of fidelity profiles: open-source community profiles for certain tasks (summarization-heavy, code-generation, customer-support).

Ending state I want to see in 3 months: basic console + SDK toggles, 2 small customer pilots, clear telemetry, and decision on billing model.

Random notes/brain dump end. Keep this file as messy scratchpad; will move to proper PRD if we decide to pursue.
